title: Potato-Tofu Vegan Unagi (Eel) Substitute with Nori Wrap
summary: This Goodful video demonstrates a plant-based eel substitute built from mashed potatoes and pressed tofu bound with cornstarch. The creator peels and cooks russet potatoes, blends them into a puree, drains moisture, and then combines the potato puree with pressed tofu. A cornstarch slurry acts as a binder, after which a portion is wrapped with a halved nori sheet. The mixture is cooked on the stove and finished with a glaze-style sauce composed of mirin, soy, sugar, kombu dashi, and maple syrup, reduced until bubbly. The host notes the texture is pleasantly bouncy and comparatively affordable, but cautions that it may not convincingly taste like eel. The method emphasizes texture and binding over flavor, with emphasis on the nori’s seaweed note and the sauce for depth.

sections.title: Potato prep and puree
sections.description: Peels russet potatoes, weighs them to match recipe units, cubes them, and blends into a puree. The liquid is drained (with options like cheesecloth or a fine sieve) to remove excess moisture, preparing the starch-lean base for binding.

sections.title: Tofu prep and binding with potato
concepts: combining dry tofu with potato puree
sections.description: Firm tofu is pressed, then combined with the dry potato puree. Salt, pepper, and a touch of soy sauce are added, followed by cornstarch to help bind the mixture before forming the shape.

sections.title: Cornstarch slurry, nori prep, and shaping
sections.description: A cornstarch slurry (cornstarch + water) is prepared as a glue. The nori sheet is split, coated with slurry, and a portion of the potato-tofu mixture is pressed onto it. The wrap is divided to create sections, with attempts to smooth lumps by blending the remainder of the mixture.

sections.title: Sauce preparation and cooking
sections.description: A sauce is assembled with mirin, soy sauce, sugar, kombu dashi, and maple syrup. The mixture is brought to a boil, then reduced until the sugar dissolves and the sauce forms large bubbles as it thickens.

sections.title: Tasting and wrap-up
sections.description: The finished product is evaluated for texture and flavor. The reviewer notes a pleasant bounce and an affordable approach, but acknowledges it may not convincingly mimic eel. Final remarks invite viewer feedback and future recipe ideas.

featured_techniques.technique: Nori sheet wrapping with slurry as adhesive
Blending remainder of mixture to smooth lumps
Sauce boiling and reduction to large bubbles
